transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Start time: 15:00 ET
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (Keystone - Head of Cloud), Miguel Reyes (Keystone - CISO), Tom Grantham (Keystone - DevOps), Sophie Lin (Keystone - Legal)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
- Keystone wants to understand data residency options for EU/US, logging restrictions for transactional data, and what controls Redwood offers for Dedicated vs Private deployments.
- Primary concerns: logs containing cardholder or personal data, auditability, key management (KMS/HSM), SSO and RBAC, plus evidence for SOC2/pen testing.

Topics: GDPR, HIPAA overlap for customer PII, SOC 2/ISO, VPC/private deployments, logging retention and redaction, default hosted vs dedicated throughput/costs.

Transcript:
00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Lena from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Marcus our solutions engineer. How's everybody doing?
00:07 Asha Patel: Good, thanks. We've got a few folks on our side. I'll kick off, we're primarily interested in how Redwood can meet our data residency and compliance needs for a small pilot first.
00:15 Marcus Chen: Great, thanks Asha. Quick agenda — understand your requirements, share how Redwood handles hosted/dedicated/private, and surface any gaps.
00:23 Miguel Reyes: Quick note, from security perspective we have pretty strict rules, we can't allow PII or transactional logs to be retained in a different jurisdiction, and we need assurances about KMS and HSM, and audit logs.
00:33 Tom Grantham: Also interested in network connectivity, whether we can do VPC peering or an on-prem appliance.
00:38 Lena Park: Totally. Maybe useful to start with your current stack and what's generating the data. What workload are you looking to run?
00:45 Asha Patel: We're looking at a customer support summarization workflow and an internal financial data assistant for advisors — both will touch sensitive customer data, some of it EU-resident.
00:55 Marcus Chen: Understood. For Hosted API we have region controls, but for strict residency we usually recommend Dedicated or Private. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity in a region and isolation, Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC or on-prem.
01:10 Miguel Reyes: Is Dedicated single-tenant? Meaning the compute and logs never leave our tenant?
01:17 Marcus Chen: Dedicated is single-tenant at the cluster level; compute doesn't mix with other customers. For logs, by default we can configure where logs are stored — e.g., S3 buckets in your account or in region-specific storage. We do have some central control plane telemetry but it can be minimized or disabled for Private.
01:36 Sophie Lin: We need to understand what telemetry Redwood keeps centrally. Any user prompts, transcripts, or embeddings — are those cached centrally by default? We have strict logging restrictions.
01:45 Marcus Chen: Good question. For Hosted the default is that inputs and outputs are processed in the region but metadata sometimes flows to our control plane for observability. For Dedicated, we can configure log forwarding to your buckets with redaction. For Private deployments the control plane can be self-hosted in your environment so minimal telemetry leaves the environment. I'll caveat that some operational metrics for the managed control plane are necessary unless you run fully private.
02:05 Lena Park: To add, we offer configurable retention windows and automatic redaction rules for PII — you can drop logs, hash identifiers, or stream sanitized logs to your storage. We also support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations.
02:18 Miguel Reyes: KMS integration — can we bring our keys? We need to ensure keys never leave our HSM.
02:24 Marcus Chen: Yes, we support BYOK patterns. For Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM directly; for Dedicated we can support customer KMS in many cloud setups. If you require HSM-managed unwrap operations within your network, that's usually part of the Private/on-prem option.
02:40 Asha Patel: GDPR-wise, our legal team will want data residency guarantees for EU subjects and a data processing addendum. Can Redwood sign?
02:48 Lena Park: We have a standard DPA and can provide EU region deployments. For enterprise customers we can negotiate specific clauses; we also provide breach notification SLAs and data deletion processes.
02:59 Sophie Lin: And pen test reports and SOC 2? We need to feed those to our InfoSec intake.
03:04 Lena Park: Absolutely. We'll include SOC 2 Type II, ISO where available, and a recent pen test summary. Full reports under NDA.
03:11 Miguel Reyes: What about logging retention and restrictions on content? For financial transactions we have to avoid storing full card numbers and certain identifiers.
03:18 Marcus Chen: We typically recommend PII redaction at the ingestion layer. We also support routing logs to your storage to enforce retention policies, and we can configure transformers to scrub fields that match regex patterns.
03:33 Tom Grantham: On the networking side — can you support private link, VPC peering, or dedicated interconnect? Latency's a factor for advisor workflows.
03:41 Marcus Chen: We support PrivateLink and VPC peering in major clouds for Dedicated. For Private/on-prem you can run within your network which gives the lowest latency. We'll share a sample diagram.
03:50 Asha Patel: Cost vs compliance tradeoffs — we need a sense of price delta between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private for the pilot. Hosted is attractive for speed but compliance may block it.
03:59 Lena Park: Right, usually Hosted is most cost-effective but least isolated; Dedicated is a middle ground with reserved capacity; Private has the highest operational overhead and cost but maximum control. We'll put together a side-by-side for a 3-month pilot.
04:11 Miguel Reyes: Are you able to sign a BAA? A couple of our products are HIPAA-adjacent and we may need a BAA.
04:18 Lena Park: We do sign BAAs for customers with HIPAA obligations in dedicated/private setups; we'll confirm exact language with legal and include in the packet.
04:27 Sophie Lin: Regarding audit logs — we need tamper-evident logs with retention policy and export capability. Can your audit trails be exported to our SIEM?
04:35 Marcus Chen: Yes, audit logs can be streamed to your SIEM (Splunk, Sumo, Azure Sentinel) and we support signed, append-only logs if you need tamper evidence; we can also integrate with your key rotation policies.
04:50 Asha Patel: Any constraints around embeddings or vector store retention? We might want to avoid storing embeddings for certain data classes.
04:58 Marcus Chen: You can configure the platform to not persist embeddings for specified routes, or store them in your own managed vector DB. We offer both: Redwood-managed embeddings with configurable retention, or you can host the embeddings store in your environment.
05:12 Miguel Reyes: What about model fallbacks? If you want to keep stuff in-region but need fallback to another model for cost/perf, does that route data out of jurisdiction?
05:20 Marcus Chen: Our smart routing will respect region and policy. If a fallback would route out-of-region, we can configure policy to prevent that, or route to a regionally-compatible model variant.
05:31 Tom Grantham: Can we run a small internal benchmark — e.g., 1000 requests, measure latency distribution for EU region — and have you help instrument that?
05:38 Lena Park: Yes, we can run a benchmark as part of the pilot. Marcus can help instrument and collect token-level latency breakdowns.
05:45 Marcus Chen: I'll propose an instrumentation plan in the tech deep dive. We'll need network egress details and representative prompts.
05:53 Sophie Lin: On the compliance intake — what's the evidence we can hand to auditors? Pen test, SOC 2, architecture diagram, KMS integration description, data flow diagrams?
06:01 Lena Park: All of the above. We'll provide an architecture diagram, dataflow, DPA, SOC 2 summary, pen test summary, and for Private deployments a deployment checklist. Full pen test reports can be shared under NDA.
06:13 Miguel Reyes: Any red flags on support for FIPS, or specific encryption suites?
06:18 Marcus Chen: We can support FIPS-compliant ciphers via your KMS/HSM; for Private/on-prem you have full control over cipher suites. For Dedicated in some clouds we can enable FIPS endpoints depending on region.
06:30 Asha Patel: How about data deletion — say a customer requests deletion of all their data in EU region — how do we handle that?
06:36 Lena Park: We have deletion APIs and can run a deletion job. For Hosted there's a standard process and timelines; for Dedicated/Private you control your storage so deletion is handled within your environment. We'll document the standard SLA for deletes.
06:48 Miguel Reyes: We also need details about who at Redwood has access to logs / plaintext. Is there human review or is it strictly automated?
06:56 Marcus Chen: Access controls are RBAC-based; for hosted managed services some ops engineers may have limited access for troubleshooting under a strict process and audit trail. For Dedicated we can restrict access further and for Private only your admins would have access. We'll include the access policy in the security pack.
07:12 Tom Grantham: Any rate-limiting or throttling we should be aware of in Dedicated? We have spiky loads during end-of-day processing.
07:19 Marcus Chen: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst capacity within policy. We can provision buffer capacity for known spikes; we'll need historical throughput numbers to size it.
07:29 Asha Patel: Let's talk timeline — we want to start a pilot in Q2, ideally end of April. Is that feasible?
07:36 Lena Park: Feasible. If you sign the pilot agreement and we get access to network contacts, we can provision a Dedicated cluster in up to 2-3 weeks; Private will take longer depending on on-prem approvals.
07:45 Sophie Lin: For the pilot agreement we will need redaction, minimum SLA, and indemnity language.
07:51 Lena Park: Understood — we'll loop legal in and include proposed clauses.
07:56 Miguel Reyes: Anything else we should surface now?
08:00 Asha Patel: One more — retention windows for logs in Europe tend to be 90 days for our use case; can you support that?
08:07 Marcus Chen: Yes, configurable retention down to 0 days for certain routes.
08:12 Lena Park: Okay, last bit — Marcus will do a tech deep dive and we'll send the security pack plus pricing for the Dedicated pilot.
08:18 Asha Patel: Sounds good. Thank you.
08:21 Miguel Reyes: Thanks everyone.
08:23 Lena Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the packet.

End of transcript.
